data.summary: test_a_long_interpreter_path_does_not_hide_the_holders_command failed in the full parallel suite: the TimeoutError had no 'Held by pid' part. _holder_note reads /proc/locks with one read_text(); the kernel serves it in several chunks and the file churns under heavy flock traffic, so entries are skipped (measured ~14% of scans miss a live holder under 40 flock churners). Silent omission, no retry, no degraded message.

data.body:
Fixes bug Bf540195aec: test_a_long_interpreter_path_does_not_hide_the_holders_command failed in the full parallel suite: the TimeoutError had no 'Held by pid' part. _holder_note reads /proc/locks with one read_text(); the kernel serves it in several chunks and the file churns under heavy flock traffic, so entries are skipped (measured ~14% of scans miss a live holder under 40 flock churners). Silent omission, no retry, no degraded message.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bf540195aec --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bf540195aec --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug Bf540195aec: lock-timeout holder note flakes under load

data.claim: /proc/locks is chunked and non-atomic, so one read skips live holders under flock churn
data.falsifier: a scan loop with 40 flock churners never misses a held lock
data.mechanism: seq_file position iteration while entries are added/removed
data.question: why does the holder section vanish under load

evidence.note: CONFIRMED: 418/3000 /proc/locks reads missed a live holder under 40 flock churners
no governing rule conflicts; change local to _holder_note
rescan with 50-scan/1s budget + still-locked probe + 'Holder unknown' message; test_lock_timeout_diagnosis+test_fsio* 135 passed -n 8; 15 runs under 60 churners clean
roborev branch review on final head fd7ddd6: 0 high/medium; 1 low (docstring 'never silence' omits the /proc/locks read-error case, theoretical) noted, not changed

chunk_findings.detail: In the pre-change code the whole scan, including `return f" Held by {_describe_pid(pid)}."`, sat inside `try: ... except (OSError, ValueError): return ""`, so any failure while describing the holder was swallowed. After the refactor, the `try` wraps only `pid = _locks_holder(want)`; the `return f" Held by {_describe_pid(pid)}."` is outside it. `_describe_pid` resolves a pid it just read from `/proc/locks` (in the bug's own scenario, the holder is a live subprocess that can exit at any moment, and under the "40 flock churners" load this change exists to survive, pid exit/reuse is routine): if that pid disappears between the `/proc/locks` read and the `/proc/<pid>/...` inspection, `_describe_pid` raises `FileNotFoundError` (an `OSError`) and it now propagates out of `_holder_note`. That happens while the `TimeoutError` for the lock is being constructed, so instead of the intended `... Held by pid N ...` message the caller gets the original `TimeoutError` replaced/chained by a `FileNotFoundError` traceback — exactly the "never raises, never masks the timeout" property this helper is documented to have, and a new way for `test_a_long_interpreter_path_does_not_hide_the_holders_command` to fail. The same applies to `ValueError` from a malformed `/proc/<pid>` read, which was also previously caught. Fix: keep the describe call inside the guarded region (or wrap it in its own `try/except (OSError, ValueError)` falling back to `_HOLDER_SCANS_MAX`/`Holder unknown`).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log.py `_holder_note` (the `return f" Held by {_describe_pid(pid)}."` line)

chunk_findings.detail: The loop turns the error-formatting path into a busy-wait that does 50 reads of `/proc/locks` plus 50 full exclusive `fsio.file_lock` acquire/release probes, and the deadline is only checked *after* each iteration and after `_locks_holder`, so the real bound is `_HOLDER_SCAN_S` (1.0 s) plus one whole scan, not 1.0 s. That cost is only avoided when the holder is visible on the first scan; in the case the new docstring explicitly promises to cover — holder in another pid namespace, `/proc/locks` present but not listing the lock (masked/empty `/proc` in a container), or `fsio.file_lock` unable to probe (ENOLCK on a flock-less mount, EACCES) where `_still_locked` answers `True` on every OSError — every single `TimeoutError` construction now blocks ~0.5–1.5 s. `_holder_note` runs *inside* the handler that builds the `TimeoutError`, so given a caller that times out under its own short deadline (a `poll_s` retry loop, a `pytest-timeout`, or the parallel suite's own per-test timeout), the outer deadline fires while the message is still being assembled, and the informative error the change exists to produce is never raised. Under the bug's own 40-flock-churner load the extra 50 scans of the kernel lock table per timeout also add the contention the retry is meant to survive.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log.py `_holder_note` (retry loop, `_HOLDER_SCANS_MAX`/`_HOLDER_SCAN_S`, `_still_locked`)

chunk_findings.detail: The retry is bypassed entirely when the read itself fails: the `except` around `pid = _locks_holder(want)` returns `""` immediately, without consulting `_still_locked` and without the new `Holder unknown (...)` message. Input: the lock is held and `/proc/locks` becomes unreadable after the `Path("/proc/locks").exists()` check (removed/masked in a container, or `read_text()` failing with EIO/ENOMEM/EMFILE under load) — `_holder_note` then silently returns `""`, which is exactly the silent omission the change declares it fixes ("a lock still held ... gives 'Holder unknown (...)', never silence"). The same hold for `ValueError` from `int(f[4])` on a malformed entry.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/infra/log.py `_holder_note` (`except (OSError, ValueError): return ""` inside the loop)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log.py `_holder_note` (`except (OSError, ValueError): return ""` inside the loop)

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier finding still holds: the refactor leaves `_describe_pid(pid)` outside the `try` that previously swallowed `OSError`/`ValueError` from describing the holder. The new regression test only manipulates the text returned for `/proc/locks` while keeping the holder process alive until `finally`; it never exercises a holder exiting between the `/proc/locks` scan and the `_describe_pid` lookup. With input where the holder pid is present in `/proc/locks` but exits before `_describe_pid` reads `/proc/<pid>/...`, `_describe_pid` can raise and that exception escapes `_holder_note` instead of producing the degraded message, so the callers do not get the intended `TimeoutError` with a note. The test’s second scenario returns an empty `/proc/locks`, which exercises the new “Holder unknown” path but not this description-failure path. This is the previous finding unchanged.
